answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can submit jobs or claim rewards. If identities are pseudonymous, creating a thousand accounts does not multiply influence: each must fund its own bond, and fraud proven through disputes burns that bond. Honest agents recover theirs, while an attacker pays real opportunity cost and risks losing capital at every identity. The stake might be denominated in copper, with timber and jade used as ordinary goods, not as extra identities.
